letter: After a licence in economics at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny, I worked for one year. I want to spend my career finding out what really causes what in messy administrative datasets. Heavy programming and abstract algorithms are not where I see myself. Markets interest me somewhat, mainly as a way to understand savings. My bachelor thesis estimated the returns to schooling with instrumental variables, and I loved every step of cleaning the census microdata.

After a licence in economics at Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny, I worked for one year. Heavy programming and abstract algorithms are not where I see myself. Regression analysis is a useful tool and I would not mind deepening it. My internship at a brokerage firm in Abidjan convinced me that volatility is the most fascinating object in economics. I have been pricing options on a spreadsheet since my second year and I follow the BRVM every day.

I completed my undergraduate studies in statistics at ISSEA. My bachelor thesis estimated the returns to schooling with instrumental variables, and I loved every step of cleaning the census microdata. Public policy questions in Africa matter to me, even if they are not my main focus. I want to spend my career finding out what really causes what in messy administrative datasets. I find algorithms elegant, although I am not a strong coder yet. I am not attracted by the world of finance and trading floors.

I graduated in applied mathematics and economics from the University of Dschang. My bachelor thesis estimated the returns to schooling with instrumental variables, and I loved every step of cleaning the census microdata. Public policy questions in Africa matter to me, even if they are not my main focus. During my internship at the national statistics institute I built a gradient-boosting model to impute missing household incomes. I am not attracted by the world of finance and trading floors.

I hold a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Yaoundé II. Markets interest me somewhat, mainly as a way to understand savings. I would like to build recommendation and allocation algorithms that are both efficient and fair. I spend my evenings on competitive programming and I recently coded a small chess engine.
